readings: For each patient sex (`Patient.SEX`), use the examination records that match a patient (drop examinations with no matching patient), first averaging each patient's examinations into one `aCL IgG` value and one `ANA` value per patient so that each patient counts once. Give the sex, the average `aCL IgG`, the average `ANA`, and that sex's average ANA divided by the mean of the per-sex average ANA values. Ignore missing values in all averages and don't round.
queries:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_igg,
        AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Examination AS e ON e.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_averages AS (
    SELECT
        SEX,
        AVG(avg_igg) AS avg_igg,
        AVG(avg_ana) AS avg_ana
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT
    SEX,
    avg_igg AS `average aCL IgG`,
    avg_ana AS `average ANA`,
    avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM sex_averages) AS `ANA ratio`
FROM sex_averages;
